_comment: `entry-a` default-imports the external through a shim tree-shaking drops, so only `entry-a` observes it as an ES module. `entry-b` merely re-exports a *named* binding, and its sole live reference lives in `referenced_symbols_by_entry_point_chunk` rather than any included statement — the one path that never reaches the inclusion pass's statement walk. It must not wrap, since observer attribution is what keeps a named-only chunk off `__toESM` (see `chunk_recorded_external_interop`), and it must not demand the helper either, or its chunk gains a cross-chunk import whose binding dies in DCE and leaves a bare `require` of the runtime chunk. Both the wrap and the runtime edge are now derived from the same observer set (`patch_module_dependencies`), which is what makes narrowing them safe on this path: `entry-b` neither wraps nor depends on the runtime, so nothing can reference a helper its chunk never imported — the panic this fixture was written to pin. With only `entry-a` demanding it, the runtime stops being shared and folds into `entry-a` outright. This pins the named-only direction; the two directions the safety argument itself rests on are pinned by `external_interop_default_reexport_only_reachable_via_entry_export` (an observer visible only as an entry export) and `external_interop_dead_default_import_keeps_helper` (a wrap that comes from the static-import channel and records no observer at all).
